issues.description: Element: Lecture constructor. The problem statement (and UML) require the constructor parameters to follow the UML attribute order: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors (see UML attribute listing). The solution implementation declares the constructor with a different parameter order: (String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents) (signature in solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13). This mismatch between the expected parameter order (per problem statement/UML) and the implemented constructor signature can confuse students mapping UML → code and may cause automated constructor-signature tests to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Either change the solution constructor signature to match the UML order: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) { ... } (and update internal assignments accordingly), or update the problem statement and UML to explicitly document the alternate parameter order used in the solution. Prefer aligning the implementation to the UML to avoid confusing students and failing constructor-signature tests.
